ai-at-work.title: The only AI glossary you’ll need this year
ai-at-work.excerpt: The rise of AI has brought an avalanche of new terms and slang. Here is a glossary with definitions of some of the most important words and phrases you might encounter.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: TechCrunch published a glossary to help people decode the explosion of AI terminology flooding the tech world right now. Digital workplace pros need this because you're going to be fielding questions from executives, employees, and vendors who are throwing around terms like "prompt engineering" and "retrieval augmented generation" without actually understanding them. Honestly, having a solid glossary bookmarked is the difference between nodding confidently in meetings and getting caught pretending you know what anyone is talking about.

ai-at-work.title: The browser wars aren’t about search anymore — here are the best alternatives to Chrome and Safari
ai-at-work.excerpt: We’ve compiled an overview of some of the top alternative browsers available today aiming to challenge Chrome and Safari.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: TechCrunch rounded up alternative browsers trying to dent Chrome and Safari's market dominance. For digital workplace folks, this matters because your browser choice directly impacts security, performance, and compatibility with your enterprise apps and collaboration tools. Look, if you're still defaulting to Chrome because IT said so in 2015, you're probably missing out on real improvements in privacy and speed that could actually make your workday less painful.

ai-at-work.title: AI data center builder Crusoe reportedly raising $3B at $30B valuation
ai-at-work.excerpt: Data center builder Crusoe Inc. is reportedly in talks to raise a $3 billion funding round. Bloomberg on Thursday cited sources as saying that the deal could value the company at $30 billion. That’s a
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Crusoe Energy, an AI data center company, is raising $3 billion at a $30 billion valuation, tripling its worth in a year. This matters because digital workplace infrastructure is increasingly dependent on AI compute capacity, and massive capital flowing into data centers signals where corporate tech spending is heading next. Look, when a company triples in value faster than your inbox fills up, someone's betting big on the infrastructure powering all those "AI-powered" tools your boss won't stop talking about.

ai-at-work.title: Meta to release new AI model with advanced coding capabilities ‘soon’
ai-at-work.excerpt: Meta Platforms Inc. is gearing up to release a new version of its flagship Muse Spark artificial intelligence model. Alexandr Wang, the company’s chief AI officer, wrote on X today that the update wil
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Meta is dropping a new version of its Muse Spark AI model with better coding chops, supposedly competitive with OpenAI's GPT-5.5, though the actual release date remains mysteriously vague. For digital workplace pros, this matters because better coding AI means your organization will need to think harder about where automation ends and human judgment begins, especially in knowledge work. The fact that Meta's chief AI officer announced this on X instead of in an actual press release tells you everything you need to know about how chaotic the AI hype cycle has become.

tools-tech.title: Meta reuses old RAM in new servers with custom bridge chip
tools-tech.excerpt: With the cost of new RAM soaring, Meta has found a thrifty way to reuse older memory in newer servers. The performance of about 40% of Meta’s millions of servers is limited by a lack of memory, the co
tools-tech.dwp_take: Meta designed a custom bridge chip to reuse older RAM modules in newer servers instead of replacing them outright, solving a cost problem created by skyrocketing memory prices. For digital workplace teams managing infrastructure costs and sustainability, this matters because it shows how even massive tech companies are feeling the pinch on hardware budgets and finding creative solutions. Here's the thing: Meta basically admitted that 40 percent of their servers are memory-constrained, which is a fancy way of saying "we've been buying servers that aren't quite right for the job" - but hey, at least they're being honest about it and fixing the problem cheaply.

tools-tech.title: Adobe premieres a second Patch Tuesday each month to deliver fixes faster
tools-tech.excerpt: Adobe will now issue security patches for its products twice as often to deal with the increasing pace of software vulnerability discovery and exploitation. This follows Oracle’s decision to increase
tools-tech.dwp_take: Adobe is adding a second Patch Tuesday on the fourth of each month to release security fixes faster, following Oracle's lead in moving to monthly patches. For digital workplace pros managing Adobe deployments across their organizations, this means twice as many update cycles to plan, test, and roll out without falling behind on security. The good news is that more frequent patches mean fewer vulnerabilities sitting around waiting to be exploited, which beats the alternative of quarterly updates by a country mile.

tools-tech.title: Meta’s AI chief says new Muse Spark update will sharpen coding, agentic AI
tools-tech.excerpt: Meta is set to launch a new Muse Spark model with stronger coding and agentic capabilities, as Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang touted the update as a step toward closing the gap with rival AI platforms
tools-tech.dwp_take: Meta is rolling out a new Muse Spark update designed to improve coding and AI agent functionality to better compete with other leading AI platforms. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because coding assistance and autonomous AI agents are becoming core productivity tools, and better performance means fewer workarounds and less time spent correcting AI outputs. Honestly, it's refreshing to see Meta focus on actually making their tools work better instead of just announcing them, though we'll believe it when we see it deployed in real enterprise environments.

tools-tech.title: Jamf exec: The exploit isn’t what gives attackers away
tools-tech.excerpt: Jamf this week unveiled Beacon, a threat-hunting service that aims to provide dedicated, proactive detection and analysis of Mac threats. The new security tool relies on Jamf’s Mac telemetry, which eq
tools-tech.dwp_take: Jamf launched Beacon, a new threat-hunting service designed to detect Mac-specific attacks through advanced telemetry and behavioral analysis rather than just looking for known exploits. For digital workplace pros managing Apple environments, this matters because most security tools still focus on Windows, leaving Mac fleets vulnerable and under-monitored. Finally, someone's building security tools for the platform we all swore wouldn't need them.

digital-culture.title: The career edge that no algorithm can take from you
digital-culture.excerpt: The narrative around artificial intelligence and work has followed a predictable arc: AI takes over tasks, humans lose jobs, and companies save money. It made intuitive sense. It also turns out to be
digital-culture.dwp_take:
Here's my response:

Big tech companies are scaling back their aggressive AI spending after realizing the efficiency gains aren't materializing as promised, and it turns out you can't just automate your way to a better business. This matters because digital workplace leaders have been under intense pressure to justify every tool purchase and every process redesign through an AI lens, when maybe the real work was just better communication and sensible workflows all along. After thirty years watching technology trends cycle through, I'm honestly relieved to see some humility returning. The best career insurance isn't learning to code or chase the latest algorithm, it's becoming someone people actually want to work with.

digital-culture.title: Panic isn’t an AI strategy
digital-culture.excerpt: Most AI “strategy” right now isn’t strategy at all. It’s a leadership response to panic. The suffocating, staring-at-the-ceiling-at-2am kind of panic that sets in when your board’s watching, your ROI
digital-culture.dwp_take: Most companies are treating AI adoption as a panic-driven scramble rather than an actual strategic plan, according to new research showing executives are under intense pressure to deploy something, anything, fast. This matters because digital workplace leaders will inherit the mess when half-baked AI implementations collide with real user needs and actual workflows. Here's the thing: your board didn't care about email management until it became a buzzword either, and we all remember how that went.

digital-culture.title: Behind the rise of the chief productivity officer and what it means for companies and employees
digital-culture.excerpt: Some employers are replacing HR directors with chief productivity officers to better align people, tech and business outcomes.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are now hiring chief productivity officers instead of traditional HR directors, betting that a tech and outcomes-focused role will better connect people strategy with business results. This matters because it signals how digital workplace tech is reshaping what leadership looks like, and whether your HR support comes from someone who gets systems thinking or just compliance boxes. Honestly, if your new CPO spends their first month trying to squeeze another 3 percent out of knowledge workers via monitoring software instead of fixing broken Slack workflows, you'll know this was just HR with a fancier title.

digital-culture.title: Can Cursor Remain a Platform for OpenAI and Anthropic’s Models Inside SpaceX?
digital-culture.excerpt: Cursor hopes to continue offering third-party AI models after it's acquired by SpaceX, testing the relationships between frontier AI labs.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Cursor, the AI code editor, is getting bought by SpaceX and wants to keep offering models from competitors like OpenAI and Anthropic instead of locking users into Elon's ecosystem. This matters because it signals whether acquired tools will stay genuinely useful or become walled gardens, which affects what developers can actually rely on long term. Honestly, I'll believe "we're staying neutral" when I see it actually happen, because nothing says "open platform" quite like being owned by the guy who names his companies after memes.

industry-news.title: AI Agents Are Creating a New Enterprise Security Gap
industry-news.excerpt: Five independent security disclosures in a single week point to the same gap: AI agent permissions, not AI agent capabilities, are the problem enterprises haven't solved. The post AI Agents Are Creati
industry-news.dwp_take: AI agents got loose with way too many permissions across five different security breaches in one week, proving the real problem isn't what these things can do but what we're letting them do. This matters because if your AI agents have blanket access to systems and data, you're basically handing hackers a skeleton key wrapped in machine learning language. After three decades watching enterprise security failures, I can tell you this is the same mistake we made with service accounts back in the 2000s, except now the account logs are written in a language nobody fully understands.

industry-news.title: Google Loses Final EU Appeal Over €4.1B Android Fine
industry-news.excerpt: Google lost its final EU appeal over a €4.1B Android fine, prompting renewed scrutiny of app defaults, search dominance, and rivals' access. The post Google Loses Final EU Appeal Over €4.1B Android Fi
industry-news.dwp_take: Google exhausted its last legal option to overturn a 4.1 billion euro fine for anticompetitive Android practices, meaning the company now has to pay up and change how it handles app defaults and search dominance in Europe. This matters because it signals regulators worldwide are serious about controlling how big tech companies lock users into their ecosystems, which directly affects the tools and integrations your organization depends on. The real takeaway is that if you've built your digital workplace strategy assuming Google's default dominance is permanent, you might want to start hedging your bets with alternative search and collaboration tools.

industry-news.title: 5 Things Google’s Nano Banana 2 Lite Reveals About the Future of AI Images
industry-news.excerpt: Google’s Nano Banana 2 Lite shows how faster, cheaper AI image generation could reshape creative workflows and business tools. The post 5 Things Google’s Nano Banana 2 Lite Reveals About the Future of
industry-news.dwp_take: Google released Nano Banana 2 Lite, a faster and cheaper AI image generation tool that signals a shift toward more accessible generative AI for everyday workflows. Digital workplace folks need to pay attention because this means image generation could soon become as standard in your content creation pipeline as spell check, which changes how teams collaborate and produce assets. Honestly, if the barrier to entry keeps dropping, companies will finally stop using those terrible stock photos from 2007, which is worth the price of admission alone.

Digital workplace pros need to pay attention because AI tools are landing in your collaboration platforms faster than your IT policies can keep up, and security gaps mean your organization's data is the prize in someone else's game. Here's the thing: every industry shift starts as a whisper in tech news before it becomes your Monday morning crisis, so staying informed beats being surprised.
